blocks.text: Psalm 88 addresses YHWH with repeated prayer, anguish, and questions, yet it offers no turn to relief or praise before it ends. The Psalter includes lament alongside petition, trust, thanksgiving, and praise; it does not treat praise as its only faithful emotional register. This helps explain why the psalm can voice its distress so directly without first softening or resolving it.

sections.title: A Psalm That Does Not Resolve Its Distress
